questions.q: What is one real problem with running an automation script only from a personal laptop?
options: Laptops are physically incapable of running PowerShell or the Azure CLI
Scripts run twice as slowly on a laptop compared to any other machine
There is no record of who ran it, when, or what happened if it quietly stops running
Git repositories cannot be cloned onto a laptop
questions.explain: Without a pipeline's logging, there is no record of execution — if the person who runs it is unavailable, nobody notices until something downstream breaks.

questions.q: Why can a script behave differently on two different laptops even though the code hasn't changed?
options: Laptops cannot run the same script more than once
The environments are inconsistent — different PowerShell or module versions can change behavior
PowerShell scripts are recompiled differently on every machine
Git automatically modifies scripts per machine
questions.explain: One machine might have PowerShell 7.4 and a newer Az module while another has older versions, causing the same script to behave differently.

questions.q: What does "logged execution" mean in the context of a CI/CD pipeline?
options: Only failed runs are recorded; successful ones are discarded
Logs are stored only on the laptop that triggered the pipeline
The pipeline requires a person to manually write a log entry after each run
Every run is automatically recorded with the triggering commit, timestamp, and full output, visible to the team later
questions.explain: A pipeline automatically records the commit, timestamp, and console output for every run, with no one needing to remember to keep notes.

questions.q: In the GitHub Actions trigger `cron: "0 7 * * MON-FRI"`, what does this configure?
options: A schedule that runs the job at 07:00 UTC every weekday
A rule that blocks the pipeline from running on weekdays
A requirement that a human approve the run every time
A trigger that only runs once, the first time it's committed
questions.explain: The cron expression "0 7 * * MON-FRI" fires the scheduled job at 07:00 UTC on Monday through Friday.

questions.q: What does `workflow_dispatch:` add to a GitHub Actions workflow?
options: An automatic rollback if the pipeline fails
A required approval step before every scheduled run
A rule that disables the schedule trigger entirely
A manual "Run workflow" button in GitHub's UI, letting someone trigger the pipeline on demand
questions.explain: workflow_dispatch adds a manual trigger button in the GitHub Actions UI, in addition to any schedule already configured.
